We need to produce a resume for Matthias Algiers. Use words with all capital letters to highlight key abilities, but ensure that words with all capital letters appear less than 10 times. So we can have maybe 5 capitalized words, each being a key ability. Must wrap the entire response with double quotation marks. So output should be a single string surrounded by double quotes. Inside, we can have line breaks? The instruction says wrap the entire response with double quotation marks. Likely they want the whole output to be a quoted string, like " ... ". Inside we can have line breaks? Usually they'd accept newline inside quotes? Might be safer to produce a single line? But a resume typically has sections separated by line breaks. We could embed \n inside the quoted string? Usually they'd want plain text with quotes at start and end. We'll output a string that starts with " and ends with ". Inside we can have line breaks; it's still part of the string. That should be fine.

We need to ensure capitalized words appear less than 10 times. We'll use maybe 6 capitalized words: LEADERSHIP, PROJECT MANAGEMENT, DATA ANALYSIS, COMMUNICATION, PROBLEM SOLVING, TECHNICAL PROFICIENCY. Each of these is a phrase with spaces; but the requirement is "words with all capital letters". Does a phrase count as multiple words? Probably each token separated by spaces is a word. So "PROJECT MANAGEMENT" contains two words: PROJECT and MANAGEMENT, both all caps. That would count as two. We need to keep total count <10. So better to use single-word capitalized abilities, like LEADERSHIP, ANALYTICS, COMMUNICATION, PROBLEMSOLVING (one word), INNOVATION, TECHNICAL. That's 6 words.

We must ensure each is all caps and appears as a separate word. We'll embed them in the resume maybe bold? But just uppercase.

We must not exceed 9 capitalized words. We'll use exactly 6.

Now craft resume: Name, contact, summary, experience, education, skills. Use capitalized words for key abilities: LEADERSHIP, ANALYTICS, COMMUNICATION, PROBLEMSOLVING, INNOVATION, TECHNICAL.

Make sure each appears only once? Could appear multiple times but each appearance counts. Safer to appear only once each. So we will include each exactly once.

Let's write:

"Matthias Algiers
Email: matthias.algiers@example.com | Phone: (555) 123-4567 | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/matthiasalgiers

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Dynamic professional with proven LEADERSHIP and ANALYTICS skills, adept at driving projects forward through effective COMMUNICATION and PROBLEMSOLVING. Passionate about INNOVATION and leveraging TECHNICAL expertise to deliver measurable results.

EXPERIENCE
Senior Project Coordinator, XYZ Corp, 2020‑Present
- Led cross‑functional teams of 10+ members, delivering projects 15% under budget.
- Utilized ANALYTICS to identify trends and improve forecasting accuracy by 20%.
- Fostered clear COMMUNICATION channels, reducing misunderstandings by 30%.
- Applied PROBLEMSOLVING frameworks to resolve critical issues swiftly.
- Championed INNOVATION initiatives that increased process efficiency by 25%.
- Applied TECHNICAL knowledge of SQL and Python to automate reporting.

Education
M.S. in Business Administration, University of State, 2018
B.S. in Computer Science, Tech Institute, 2016

SKILLS
Project Management, Data Analysis, Stakeholder Engagement, Agile Methodologies, SQL, Python, Tableau"

Now count capitalized words: LEADERSHIP (1), ANALYTICS (2), COMMUNICATION (3), PROBLEMSOLVING (4), INNOVATION (5), TECHNICAL (6). That's 6 <10.

Check that we didn't accidentally include other all caps words like "XYZ" (that's all caps but it's an acronym; it counts as a word with all caps. The instruction: "Use words with all capital letters to highlight key abilities, but make sure that words with all capital letters appear less than 10 times." It doesn't forbid other all caps words, but they'd count toward the limit. Safer to avoid any other all caps words. So we need to avoid XYZ Corp (XYZ is all caps). Also avoid "M.S."? That's not all caps because includes period and lower? Actually "M.S." has capital M and S but periods; still letters are uppercase, but might be considered a word with all capital letters? It's ambiguous. Safer to avoid any other all caps sequences. Also avoid "B.S." etc. Also avoid "SQL", "Python" (Python not all caps), "Tableau". So we need to change XYZ Corp to something like "Company ABC" but ABC is all caps. Better to use a lowercase company name: "Global Solutions Inc." but Inc is capital I then lowercase? Actually "Inc." has capital I then lowercase n c; not all caps. So we can use "Global Solutions". Avoid acronyms that are all caps. Also avoid "M.S." and "B.S." maybe use "Master of Science" and "Bachelor of Science". Those have capital M S etc but not all caps because they have lowercase letters. "Master of Science" has M capital, rest lowercase; not all caps. "Bachelor of Science" similar. So we can write those.

Also avoid "GPA"? Not needed.

We must ensure no stray all caps like "USA". Avoid.

Let's rewrite.

"Matthias Algiers
Email: matthias.algiers@example.com | Phone: (555) 123-4567 | LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/matthiasalgiers

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Dynamic professional with proven LEADERSHIP and ANALYTICS skills, adept at driving projects forward through effective COMMUNICATION and PROBLEMSOLVING. Passionate about INNOVATION and leveraging TECHNICAL expertise to deliver measurable results.

EXPERIENCE
Senior Project Coordinator, Global Solutions, 2020‑Present
- Led cross‑functional teams of 10+ members, delivering projects 15% under budget.
- Utilized ANALYTICS to identify trends and improve forecasting accuracy by 20%.
- Fostered clear COMMUNICATION channels, reducing misunderstandings by 30%.
- Applied PROBLEMSOLVING frameworks to resolve critical issues swiftly.
- Championed INNOVATION initiatives that increased process efficiency by 25%.
- Applied TECHNICAL knowledge of SQL and Python to automate reporting.

EDUCATION
Master of Science in Business Administration, University of State, 2018
Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Tech Institute, 2016

SKILLS
Project Management, Data Analysis, Stakeholder Engagement, Agile Methodologies, SQL, Python, Tableau"

Now check for any all caps words besides the six we intend.

Lines:

- "Matthias Algiers" - both capitalized first letters but not all caps.
- "Email:" - E capital, rest lowercase.
- "matthias.algiers@example.com" - lowercase.
- "Phone:" - P capital, rest lowercase.
- "(555) 123-4567" - numbers.
- "LinkedIn:" - L capital, rest lowercase? Actually "LinkedIn:" has L capital, i n k e d I n? Actually "LinkedIn" has capital L and I at end? It's mixed case; not all caps.
- "PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY" - all caps! That's two words: PROFESSIONAL and SUMMARY. Both all caps. That would add to count. We need to avoid any all caps words besides our six. So we need to change section headings to not be all caps. Use title case maybe: "Professional Summary". That's not all caps. Similarly "Experience", "Education", "Skills". Also "Senior Project Coordinator" - "Senior" capital S, rest lowercase; "Project" capital P; "Coordinator" capital C. Those are not all caps because they have lowercase letters. Good.

But we have "Global Solutions" - G capital, S capital, rest lowercase; not all caps.

We need to check lines for any accidental all caps like "SQL" - that's all caps (three letters). SQL is all caps and would count as a word. We used SQL in the SKILLS line and also in experience line: "Applied TECHNICAL knowledge of SQL and Python". SQL is all caps. That would add to count. We need to avoid SQL or count it but keep total <10. We have six already; adding SQL would make 7, still <10. But we also have "Python" (not all caps). "Tableau" not all caps. So we could keep SQL, it's okay as long as total <10. However we also have "USA"? Not present. We also have "M.S." removed. Good.

But we need to check if any other all caps like "IT"? Not present.
